Other categories such as dry goods, canned goods, meat, alcohol, and international foods also show minimal presence.

title: High Volume, Diverse Product Shoppers
description: This cluster represents shoppers with a significantly higher number of unique products and total products purchased. They also place more orders frequently, indicating strong engagement. Their purchasing habits span a wide variety of aisles and departments, suggesting diverse interests and needs.

title: Dominant Bakery, Few Unique Products
description: This cluster is heavily dominated by the bakery department, representing a significant portion of its offerings. In contrast, it features a very low variety of unique products and a limited number of unique aisles. The cluster also shows minimal presence in pet, bulk, and international sections, with a complete absence of these categories.

title: Bakery Focused, Low Volume Shoppers
description: This cluster shows a significantly higher proportion of bakery items purchased compared to the global average. Conversely, they buy fewer total products and unique items. Their purchasing behavior indicates a niche focus, potentially with fewer overall shopping trips.

title: Pets and Household Essentials Focus
description: This cluster shows a strong emphasis on pet supplies, significantly exceeding the global average. Household goods and personal care items are also purchased more frequently than average. Conversely, produce and bulk items are bought less often, and the total number of products and orders are lower.

title: Weekend shoppers, focus on canned goods
description: This cluster primarily shops on weekends, with a notable preference for Saturdays and Sundays. They show a significantly higher proportion of purchases in canned goods compared to the global average. Conversely, there's a lower engagement with baby products, alcohol, pets, and household items.

title: Larger Baskets, Less Frequent, No Alcohol
description: This cluster demonstrates significantly larger average basket sizes compared to the global mean. Customers in this group order far less frequently and do not purchase alcohol. They show a slight increase in dry goods and pasta, with minimal spending in other diverse departments.

title: Unusual Purchases: High 'Other', Low Variety
description: This cluster shows a significant overrepresentation of 'other' departments, suggesting unusual or unclassified purchases. There's also a slight increase in baby and alcohol product percentages. Conversely, customers in this cluster buy significantly fewer unique products and fewer total items, indicating a preference for specialized or limited shopping.

title: Bulk and Snack Focused, Fewer Unique Products
description: This cluster shows a significant increase in bulk and snack purchases compared to the global average.  Conversely, there's a notable decrease in unique products purchased. The cluster also exhibits lower spending on babies, alcohol, and household categories.

title: Produce Dominant, Minimal Other Departments
description: This cluster heavily emphasizes produce, making up over half of its sales. Conversely, departments like pets, babies, and alcohol are virtually absent. Other categories such as international, bulk, and personal care also show significantly lower representation. This suggests a specialized store focusing primarily on fresh goods.

title: High Bakery Sales, High Reorder Rate
description: This cluster exhibits a significantly higher proportion of sales from the bakery department.  It also shows a considerably elevated reorder rate and a greater number of total orders.  Departments like pets, babies, and alcohol have a negligible presence.

title: Frozen Focus, Lower Purchase Volume
description: This cluster strongly favors frozen items, with a much higher percentage than the global average. They tend to buy fewer products and place fewer orders overall. Despite the lower volume, their purchase frequency is remarkably consistent.

title: Frequent Buyers of Diverse Products
description: This cluster represents customers who purchase a significantly higher number of total and unique products. They also exhibit a larger average basket size and explore a wider variety of unique aisles and departments.  These shoppers consistently reorder items and show a slight preference for pasta and baby products, while avoiding alcohol purchases.

title: Weekend Shoppers, Pantry & Frozen Focus
description: This cluster strongly favors weekend shopping, indicated by a significantly higher preferred day of the week. They also show a heightened preference for pantry staples and frozen goods. While they purchase fewer total products and orders, their reorder rate suggests loyalty to these specific departments.

title: High Dairy & Egg, High Order Volume
description: This cluster exhibits a significantly higher proportion of dairy and egg purchases. Customers in this group also place considerably more orders and purchase more products per order. The reorder rate is notably high, suggesting strong customer loyalty. Conversely, categories like pets, meat, canned goods, and baby products are underrepresented.

title: Personal Care & Household Focus
description: This cluster heavily emphasizes personal care and household products, significantly exceeding global averages.  It shows a moderate focus on beverages while having less representation in produce, meat, and alcohol. Other categories are minimal or absent.

title: International Baby & Specialty Shoppers
description: This cluster represents shoppers with a strong preference for international products, buying significantly more than the global average. They also show a higher inclination towards baby products. Conversely, they purchase far fewer total and unique products, suggesting a focused shopping basket.  The absence of alcohol, bulk, and other specific categories further defines their purchasing behavior.

title: Less Frequent Orders, More Pantry Items
description: This cluster represents shoppers who order less frequently than average. They tend to purchase a higher proportion of pantry staples, canned goods, and fresh meat/seafood.  Conversely, they buy significantly fewer items from the bulk, babies, and general grocery aisles.

title: High Meat & Seafood, Low Overall Purchase
description: This cluster represents customers with a strong preference for meat and seafood departments. They purchase significantly fewer unique products and have a smaller average basket size. Overall purchase volume and variety are substantially lower compared to the global average.

title: Frequent, Diverse, and Loyal Shoppers
description: This cluster represents highly active customers who place significantly more orders and purchase a greater variety of products. They exhibit a strong tendency to reorder items, indicating high loyalty. Their purchasing behavior spans across personal care, pets, and household departments, suggesting diverse needs.

title: Breakfast Dominant, Few Other Categories
description: This cluster is overwhelmingly characterized by a high percentage of breakfast items. Conversely, it shows very low or no representation in categories like bulk, babies, and international products. The overall product diversity and purchase volume are significantly lower than the global average, indicating a specialized, focused purchasing behavior.

title: Beverage & Snacks Dominant, Other Categories Absent
description: This cluster is heavily dominated by a high percentage of sales in beverages and snacks.  Conversely, categories like pets, babies, canned goods, and international foods are virtually non-existent.  Other departments like meat, frozen, and bakery also show significantly lower contributions.

title: Early Morning Non-Alcohol Shoppers
description: This cluster represents shoppers who consistently purchase in the early morning hours, avoiding alcohol and baby items. They show a higher percentage of purchases in dry goods and pasta. While their total orders are lower, their average basket size is significantly larger.

title: Snack Focused, Infrequent Shoppers
description: This cluster exhibits a strong preference for snacks, which represent a significantly higher proportion of their purchases. They order much less frequently than the average customer. The number of unique products purchased is also considerably lower.

title: Dominant Household Goods Retailers
description: This cluster is defined by an exceptionally high percentage of household product sales. Conversely, these retailers have minimal sales in perishable departments like deli, meat, frozen, and produce. They also show significantly lower percentages in dry goods, pasta, canned goods, and dairy/eggs compared to the global average. This suggests a focus on non-food household essentials.

title: Produce-Dominant Stores with Many Items
description: This cluster represents stores with a significantly higher number of products per aisle compared to the global average. They heavily emphasize the produce department, dedicating a substantial portion of their offerings to it. Notably, these stores appear to completely exclude or have very minimal representation in categories like bulk, bakery, babies, pets, meat, seafood, alcohol, and dry goods/pasta.

title: Large Baskets, Infrequent Buyers
description: This cluster exhibits significantly larger average basket sizes compared to the global mean. Customers in this group tend to order much less frequently, with longer intervals between purchases. They show a notable absence of alcohol and bulk item purchases.

title: High Product Variety, Large Baskets
description: This cluster exhibits a significantly higher number of unique products and aisles per customer compared to the global average. Customers in this cluster also purchase a larger total quantity of products and tend to have larger basket sizes.  Interestingly, there's a notable decrease in alcohol purchases, while canned goods show a slight increase.

title: High Personal Care, Household Goods Focus
description: This cluster exhibits an exceptionally high proportion of personal care items, significantly above the global average. It also shows a notable concentration in household goods and a smaller presence in 'other' categories. Conversely, departments like deli, international, bakery, meat, produce, and dry goods are underrepresented.

title: High Pasta, Low Alcohol & Babies
description: This cluster shows a strong preference for pasta within dry goods, significantly deviating from the global average. Conversely, departments like alcohol, babies, and pets are notably underrepresented. Shopping behavior indicates a preference for weekdays over weekends.

title: Low Bulk, Baby, Pet, Alcohol Purchase Cluster
description: This cluster exhibits a significantly higher proportion of international departments compared to the global average. Conversely, it shows notably lower purchasing activity in bulk, baby, pet, and alcohol categories. Customers in this cluster also tend to make fewer total orders and purchase fewer products overall. Their reorder rate is lower, but their purchase frequency consistency is higher.

title: Frequent Dairy/Egg Buyers, Infrequent Orders
description: This cluster exhibits a significantly higher proportion of dairy and egg purchases compared to the global average. Conversely, they place fewer total orders and have a longer average time between orders.  They also show substantially less purchasing in many other departments, suggesting a specialized buying pattern focused on fresh items.

title: High Bulk, Low Alcohol, Frequent Buyers
description: This cluster represents frequent buyers who purchase a significant percentage of bulk items. They show a high reorder rate and buy more products per order compared to the global average. Notably, their spending on alcohol and household supplies is lower than expected.

title: Produce Focus, Lower Order Frequency
description: This cluster shows a significant emphasis on produce, representing a much larger proportion of purchases. Conversely, there's a notable underrepresentation of departments like alcohol, household, and personal care. Customers in this cluster tend to have a lower total number of orders. They also exhibit higher hour consistency, suggesting more predictable shopping times.

title: High Bulk and Snacks, Few Unique Items
description: This cluster is characterized by a disproportionately high percentage of bulk items and snacks purchased. Conversely, customers in this cluster buy significantly fewer unique products. Departments like pets, babies, and international goods are virtually absent from their purchases. The total number of products purchased is also considerably lower than the global average.

title: Frequent Beverage & Other Buyers
description: This cluster shows a strong preference for beverages and 'other' departments, significantly exceeding global averages. Customers here also show higher spending in personal care and household items. They tend to purchase fewer unique products and have smaller basket sizes compared to the average shopper.

title: Average Spending, High Unique Products
description: This cluster represents customers with purchasing habits very close to the global average. They buy a slightly higher number of unique products and have a marginally larger basket size. Their spending in departments like bulk, other, alcohol, and personal care is notably lower than average.
